Lenses change the shape of the cornea and can affect the measurements used to choose your lens implant. Stop soft lenses at least 1 week before, and rigid (RGP) lenses at least 2–3 weeks before, unless the clinic advises otherwise. Bring your glasses instead.
Sudden vision loss, a painful red eye, or an eye injury? Do not wait for a clinic day. Go to the nearest emergency department or call 1669.

Dr Somkijrungroj graduated from Phramongkutklao College of Medicine, Bangkok, in 2004, served as a medical officer in the Royal Thai Army (2004–2007) and completed his ophthalmology residency at Rajavithi Hospital, Bangkok (2007–2010, best resident award). He trained in retina and vitreous at Chulalongkorn University (2011–2012) and, as an international fellow of the Francis I. Proctor Foundation, University of California, San Francisco, in uveitis and in medical cornea and external disease (2013–2014). He joined the faculty of Chulalongkorn University in 2012 and has led its uveitis unit since; he trains two to three retina fellows each year and opened the university’s uveitis fellowship in 2017.

His practice spans advanced and complicated cataract surgery, uveitis, and medical and surgical retina. His research interests include presbyopia-correcting IOL optics and digital reading performance with multifocal lenses, immediate sequential bilateral cataract surgery, imaging in uveitis and retina, diagnostic tests for uveitis, CMV keratouveitis, ocular Behçet disease and infectious uveitis, and intravitreal drug-delivery devices.

He founded the Chula–KKU–Proctor–UCSF (CKPU) conference (first meeting January 2017), heads the information technology committees of the Royal College of Ophthalmologists of Thailand (2020–present) and the Thailand Ocular Immunology and Inflammation Society (2014–present), and served on the committee of the Thai Retina Society (2018–2020). He is an APACRS Certified Educator (2026) and a regular faculty member at APACRS, APAO, APVRS, ESCRS, IOIS and the Royal College meetings.
